title: Milestone: The Age of Pyramids
objective: After this level you can connect the pharaohs, pyramids, gods and writing of Egypt’s first great age.
summary: In the 24th century BCE, Unas became the first king to fill his pyramid with writing: the Pyramid Texts, Egypt’s oldest surviving religious writings, where pharaoh, pyramid, gods and writing meet.

cards.headline: Milestone: halfway to Mastery. Let’s read the walls of a pyramid.
cards.body: Egypt’s first great age was the age of the great pyramids. For generations, no king wrote on the walls inside. Then one king became the first to fill his pyramid with writing.

events.label: The age of the great pyramids at Giza
Unas has the first Pyramid Texts carved in his pyramid

cards.headline: The Pyramid Texts
cards.body: Unas, last king of the 5th Dynasty, was the first pharaoh to inscribe the inside of his pyramid at Saqqara. His Pyramid Texts are prayers, hymns and spells meant to protect a dead king or queen and ensure life and food in the hereafter. Several more pyramids at Saqqara followed his lead. Together they are the oldest surviving body of Egyptian religious writing. Pharaoh, pyramid, gods and writing, all in one room.

cards.headline: Milestone: writing and knowledge
learned: Unas first filled a pyramid with writing, the Pyramid Texts
They are Egypt’s oldest surviving religious writings
They were carved in the Old Kingdom, 24th century BCE
Writing, math, the calendar and medicine made Egypt a land of knowledge

questions.prompt: Writing and Knowledge recap: why is “picture writing” the wrong name for hieroglyphs?

options.label: They had no pictures at all
options.rationale: Hieroglyphs were full of pictures.

options.label: Most signs stood for sounds, not the things they showed
Only priests were allowed to call them pictures
options.rationale: No such rule existed.

options.label: They were always written in columns
options.rationale: They could run in rows or columns.

questions.explanation: Hieroglyphs could show what they pictured, but most signs stood for sounds of one to three consonants.

questions.prompt: Egyptian calendar recap: how many days did the civil year have?

options.rationale: That’s close to a lunar year.
360 leaves out the 5 extra days.
There was no leap day.

questions.explanation: Twelve months of 30 days plus five extra days made 365.

questions.prompt: Egyptian math recap: which kind of fraction did scribes work with, apart from two-thirds?

options.label: Decimals, like 0.5
options.rationale: Egyptians didn’t use decimals.

options.label: Percentages
options.rationale: Percentages weren’t used.

options.label: Unit fractions, with 1 on top
Fractions with 10 on the bottom only
options.rationale: The rule was about the top number.

questions.explanation: Scribes wrote fractions as unit fractions, with 1 as the numerator; two-thirds was the exception.

questions.prompt: What were the Pyramid Texts in Unas’s pyramid meant to do?

options.label: Record how much the pyramid cost to build
options.rationale: They are religious texts, not accounts.

options.label: Teach young scribes how to write hieratic
options.rationale: They were for the dead king, not a school.

options.label: List the taxes owed by every province
options.rationale: They are spells and hymns, not tax lists.

options.label: Protect the dead king in the hereafter

questions.explanation: They are prayers, hymns and spells to protect a dead king or queen and ensure life and sustenance in the hereafter.

questions.prompt: Medical papyri recap: how does the Ebers Papyrus differ from the Edwin Smith injury cases?

options.label: Ebers is packed with magical formulas and folk remedies
Ebers deals only with broken bones
options.rationale: That is closer to the Smith cases.

options.label: Ebers contains no remedies at all
options.rationale: It holds hundreds of remedies.

options.label: Ebers was written 1,000 years later, in Greek
options.rationale: Both are Egyptian papyri of about the same era.

questions.explanation: The Smith cases are chiefly practical; the Ebers Papyrus holds hundreds of magical formulas and folk remedies.

questions.prompt: In which of Level 1’s kingdoms were the first Pyramid Texts carved?

options.label: The Old Kingdom
The Middle Kingdom
options.rationale: Unas lived long before the Middle Kingdom.

options.label: The New Kingdom
options.rationale: The New Kingdom was about a thousand years later.

options.label: None: they came after Roman rule
options.rationale: They are from the pharaohs’ own age.

questions.explanation: Unas carved them in the 24th century BCE, inside the Old Kingdom (about 2686 to 2160 BCE).

questions.prompt: Scribes and papyrus recap: hieratic was written on papyrus. What held a papyrus sheet together?

options.label: Stitches of linen thread
options.rationale: The sheets weren’t sewn.

options.label: The plant’s own sap, pressed in
A coat of melted beeswax
options.rationale: No wax was needed.

options.label: A thin wash of wet clay
options.rationale: The plant’s sap did the gluing.

questions.explanation: Pressing the damp, crossed strips let the papyrus sap glue them; scribes wrote hieratic on the finished sheets.
